Our coach wording (ours, unreviewed) for the revised review-level A02 activity built with the PROPOSED configuration A02-HPE2, for Christian's ecological review. Read only by unit tests, through the tests-only reader back/src/system/rendering/candidate-coach-wording.ts, and handed to a TEST-ONLY build (build-activity.ts candidateWording) beside the approved table, never in it. No route, no engine module and no approved table reads it; nothing here is in approved-coach-wording.json or draft-coach-wording.json.
label: CANDIDATE
about: Package 5, the A02 ecological revision (13 November 2026), on Christian's reply received 13 November 2026, heading 6: concise Setup, Rules, Scoring and Learning Explanation sections, technical qualifications kept in the representation, the existing approved coach translation used, no prescription for defensive behaviour. One entry, in the approved table's cover shape with candidateBy in place of an approval, says the escaping team's scoring and its condition once, matched to the exact values the realized A02-HPE2 game holds (the revised origin and progression values of a02-hpe2-composition; the marked line PROPOSED in a02-proposed/hpe2.PROPOSED.json); a value that drifts no longer matches, the field is withheld and the build refuses (fail closed). The printed-only sentences give the rest of the coach text, each standing for the engine sentences it states in fewer words (standsFor, by their exact text), so the review print prints every engine sentence exactly once. Where the engine cannot say what our draft said, the text follows the engine and the difference is recorded in the HPE-2 evidence: no block clock (the engine says there is no set block length), no rule for where opponents stand at a restart (no register row), and the coach's restart in the engine's broad words with an example of when it helps. The learning explanation is printed by the review print from knowledge (the Learning Goal's Coach Definition and RPC-STMT-010, High Press Escape's coach translation), never from this file. No template: both teams' targets are zones, which the production renderer says in its own words.

match.equals: established coordinated pressure, encountered and then escaped by this crossing

equals.asAuthored: the pressing line, as the marked line PROPOSED in A02-HPE2 (N1)

match.equals: retains possession through the next action

entries.sentence: The escaping team scores a point when, in an attempt that starts with the pressing team pressing together, a player dribbles over the line, or receives and controls the ball beyond it, and the team keeps the ball through its next action. One player closing down alone does not necessarily count as pressing together. No point if play stops first; use your judgment for unusual stoppages.
standsFor: Escaping team: Score by getting the ball under control into its target zone: running it in, or passing to a teammate who receives it under control inside
Mark the escaping team's target zone from the marked line to the pressing team's end line, across the full width

restates.words: The sequence begins under established coordinated pressure, the event occurs beyond the pressing line, and the attacking team retains possession through the next action.

rulings.quote: A qualifying sequence begins when the attacking team possesses the ball while facing established, coordinated defensive pressure.
An isolated defender closing down the ball does not necessarily constitute coordinated pressure.
We shouldn't require the press to remain intact after it has been broken.
Whose action: The attacking team's next relevant ball action following completion of the scoring event.
If play stops first: Ordinarily the continuation requirement has not been completed, so the point has not yet been earned.
Practical exceptions involving unusual stoppages should remain subject to reasonable coach judgment rather than an elaborate universal rule.
The important relationship is between encountering established coordinated pressure and subsequently escaping it while preserving attacking continuity.
Facing coordinated pressure earlier in possession should not automatically qualify an unrelated later scoring event.
Please preserve that distinction without introducing unnecessary phase machinery or elaborate referee-like conditions for coaches.

printerOnly.label: CANDIDATE
printerOnly.sentence: Mark out an area 40 m long by 30 m wide. Play 6 v 6, no goalkeepers, for 18 minutes.
standsFor: Mark out an area 40 m long by 30 m wide
Divide 12 players into 2 teams of 6, with no goalkeepers

rulings.quote: Setup: What the coach needs to arrange.
I would prefer concise Setup, Rules, Scoring and Learning Explanation sections, with technical qualifications kept in the underlying representation where possible.

printerOnly.label: PROPOSED
printerOnly.sentence: At one end, mark a full-width end zone 6 m deep, and a full-width line 12 m from that end line.
standsFor: Mark a line across the area, 12 m from the escaping team's end line
Mark the pressing team's target zone at the escaping team's end, 6 m deep, across the full width

rulings.quote: Where a marked reference is necessary, its position should serve the intended game problem rather than become an arbitrary geometric requirement.
I'd like the next package to examine whether a more coherent relationship between defensive rewards, attacking targets and possession consequences would better support the learning intention.

printerOnly.label: PROPOSED
printerOnly.sentence: The team defending that end is the escaping team; the other is the pressing team. Swap roles when you choose: the teams change ends and the markings stay.
standsFor: Play in blocks: in each block one team is the escaping team and the other is the pressing team

When you call the next block the teams change ends and exchange roles: each role is played from the same end in every block, so each team now attacks the target zone of its new role; there is no set block length
Each team attacks the zone at the other team's end. Decide which team starts at which end

rulings.quote: I am comfortable retaining asymmetric escaping and pressing roles as a review-level candidate, including exchanging roles between blocks.
"Pressing team" is an acceptable role description.

printerOnly.label: PROPOSED
printerOnly.sentence: Start, and restart after each point, with an escaping player on the ball near their own end, outside the end zone, where you choose. You may also restart this way whenever you judge an attempt has run its course, for example when the escaping team holds the ball beyond the line unpressed.
standsFor: A player of the escaping team restarts play: at the start, after either team scores and whenever you decide that an attack has run its course (at a stoppage or while play is on)
A player of the escaping team restarts play from the feet, with the ball still or moving
You choose where a player of the escaping team restarts play, near the escaping team's own end, outside the end zone

rulings.quote: A representative coach-managed restart can be useful when the activity needs to recreate the relevant pressure situation, but it should not automatically become the only permitted way a qualifying sequence begins.
I would avoid instructions such as "set to press together" if they become prescriptions for defensive behavior rather than descriptions of a representative starting condition.

printerOnly.label: PROPOSED
printerOnly.sentence: If the ball goes over an end line, the team that did not touch it last restarts from the feet: the escaping team as at the start, the pressing team on the line, where you choose. Throw-ins and free kicks as normal; no offside.
standsFor: If the ball goes out over either end line, a player of the team that did not touch the ball last restarts play, from the feet, with the ball still or moving; you choose where (for the escaping team near its own end, outside the end zone; for the pressing team on the marked line)

rulings.quote: My preference remains to preserve meaningful possession consequences and reasonable coach discretion.
For now, no offside may remain an isolated review assumption, but I am not approving it as a general A02 rule.
The normal Laws of the Game should apply by default wherever they are applicable, unless an activity introduces an explicit, knowledge-authorized modification.

printerOnly.label: PROPOSED
printerOnly.sentence: The pressing team scores a point when a player dribbles into the end zone, or receives and controls the ball inside it. Points from both roles add up; most points wins.
standsFor: Pressing team: Score by getting the ball under control into its target zone: running it in, or passing to a teammate who receives it under control inside

rulings.quote: Second, the pressing team's only scoring option—dribbling over the opponent's end line—may unnecessarily narrow its attacking solutions.
If both teams understand the rules and genuinely attempt to win, do their available opportunities and incentives make the intended learning problem likely to emerge?
